source_text:
Dedit ergo Deus bonum, quemadmodum et Apostolus testificatur in eadem epistola, et qui operantur quidem illud, gloriam et honorem percipient, quoniam operati sunt bonum cum possint non operari illud; hi autem qui illud non operantur, judicium justum excipient Dei, quoniam non sunt operati bonum cum possint operari illud.

Ostensio quod non natura quidam boni sint, quidam vero mali, sed quod in hominis electione sit bonum.
pass_a_gloss: God gave the good; workers of good get glory because they could have not worked it; non-workers judged because they could have; good is in human choice not fixed natures.
pass_b_english: God gave the good, as the apostle also testifies in the same letter. Those who work it will receive glory and honor, because they worked the good when they were also able not to work it.

Those who do not work it will receive God’s just judgment, because they did not work the good when they were able to work it. The showing is not that some are good by nature and others evil, but that the good lies in human choice.

choices.choice: able not to work it / in human choice
choices.why: Re-audit required Pass B to stay inside the locked block; counsel material is the next section.

variants.note: Greek fragment (Joh. Damasc.) interleaves in Harvey scan; Latin AH is the lock.

anf_compare.notes: Sense matches ANF 4.37.4; English constrained to continuous Latin.
